title: Kidney beans, from dried, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: Kidney beans are dried red beans that contain no added fat. After drying they retain high levels of protein, fiber, and complex carbohydrates. The beans are typically boiled before eating, making them a versatile ingredient for soups, stews, salads, and vegetarian dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The name "kidney bean" comes from its reddish‑brown color and kidney‑like shape.
The beans are rich in antioxidants, especially flavonoids that give them their vivid hue.
Dried beans can be stored for up to a year in a cool, dry place.
Kidney beans are a staple in Latin American, Mediterranean, and Asian cuisines.
Soaking dried beans for 4–12 hours before cooking reduces cooking time and improves digestibility.

items.title: Rich source of plant protein
items.content: A 100‑g serving of dry beans provides about 24 g of protein, making it valuable for vegetarians and vegans.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports healthy digestion, promotes satiety, and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Contains iron and folate
items.content: Beans supply iron for oxygen transport and folate essential for DNA synthesis.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Dried kidney beans contain virtually no fat, fitting well into calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Potassium and magnesium in beans help maintain healthy blood pressure.

items.title: Toxic compounds in raw beans
items.content: Raw kidney beans contain phytohaemagglutinin, a toxic glycoside. It must be destroyed by boiling for at least 10 minutes.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to legumes.

items.title: Gas and bloating
items.content: Beans can cause increased gas in sensitive people; proper soaking and cooking reduce this effect.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Soak dried beans in water for 4–12 hours, drain, then boil for 60–90 minutes until tender. Cooked kidney beans are used in chili, soups, salads, veggie burgers, and as a side dish.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dried beans in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. Properly stored they keep quality for up to 12 months. Cooked beans can be refrigerated for 4‑5 days.
